texts.preamble: P.K.Kunhumuhammed vs State Of Kerala on 22 January, 2025 Crl.Rev.Pet No. 970 Of 2013 1 2025:Ker:4863 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr.Justice K. V. Jayakumar Wednesday, The 22Nd Day Of January 2025 / 2Nd Magha, 1946 Crl.Rev.Pet No. 970 Of 2013 Against The Order/Judgment Dated 27.04.2013 In Crl.A No.245 Of 2011 Of Additional Sessions Court, (Adhoc-I), Kalpetta, Wyanad Arising Out Of The Order/Judgment Dated In Cc No.374/2008 Of Judicial Magistrate Of First Class ,Sulthanbathery Revision Petitioner/Appellant/1St Accused: P.K.Kunhumuhammed S/O.Abdu, Pullanikkattil House, Kalloor, Noolpuzha Village, Sulthanbathery, Wayanad District. By Adv Sri.Nirmal V Nair Respondent/Complainant/State: State Of Kerala Represented By Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam-682031. By Advs. Advocate General Office Kerala Addl. Director General Of Prosecution(Ag-11)
texts.facts: This revision petition is preferred against the judgment of the Additional Sessions Court (Adhoc-1), Kalpetta, Wayanad in Crl.A.No.245 of 2011. 2. The brief facts necessary for the disposal of this criminal revision are as follows: The revision petitioner herein was the appellant in Crl.A.No.245/2011 on the file of Additional Sessions Court (Adhoc)-I, Kalpetta and accused in C.C.No.374/2008 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Sulthan Bathery. The offences alleged against the accused are under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) r/w section 7(ii) and (iii) r/w Section 2(ix)(k) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred as "the Act") r/w Rule 32(c) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and u/s 16(1)(a)(i) r/w Section 7(iii) Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. 3. The allegation in the complaint was that, on 28.02.2008 at about 2.30 pm PW1, the Food Inspector of Kalpetta Circle, purchased 6 bottles of soft drink named 'Mirinda' from the shop namely "Kabani Bakery" functioning in 2025:KER:4863 Door No.IV/677 situated at Kaloor in Noolpuzha Grama Panchayath after complying the formalities. When one of the samples was sent to the public analyst, it was reported that the sample was misbranded. Thus the 1 st accused has committed the offences alleged against him.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the revision petitioner placing reliance on the decision reported in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and Another (2010 (4) KHC 767) submitted that the impugned judgment is legally unsustainable. 9. In Pepsico's case (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court absorbed that in the absence of Rules framed by the Central Government defining the Laboratories where samples of food could be analysed and in the absence of prescribing validated methods of analysis, no prosecution can continue under the Act. Paragraphs 38 and 39 of the 2025:KER:4863 said judgment reads as follows: 38. It is now well established that in a complaint against a Company and its Directors, the P.K.Kunhumuhammed vs State Of Kerala on 22 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106974850/ 3 A mere bald statement that a person was a Director of the Company against which certain allegations had been made is not sufficient to make such Director liable in the absence of any 2025:KER:4863 specific allegations regarding his role in the management of the Company." 10. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has also placed reliance on the decision reported in Rasheed N.K. v. Food Inspector, Thalassery and another (2016 (2) KHC 679). In Rasheed's case (supra) it was held that the ratio in Pepsico's case (supra), can be applied to all cases of alleged food adulteration under the Act irrespective of the fact whether or not standards have been prescribed for food items. "18. Bearing in mind the fact that the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pepsico's case (supra) held that the provisions under Section 23(I-A) (ee) and (hh) are not directory and that this court has erred in holding that they are only enabling provisions we will proceed further to answer the referred questions. It is to be noted that after the decision in Pepsico's case (supra) by the Hon'ble Apex Court a notification was followed whereby Rule in relation to Section 23(IA) (hh) was framed as Rule 4 (9) of the PFA Rules.
